description: A hugely significant and monumental site on a hilltop west of Armagh, that shows repeated re-use and modification from the Late Bronze Age, through the Iron Age, to the Medieval Period. Beginning as a hilltop Late Bronze age enclosure, in the Iron Age repeated huge figure-of-eight structures were built, before a large round roofed structure was built, filled with stone, burnt down, and covered in turf to create the mound known as Site B. Around this time another figure-of-eight structure was built just to the west (Site A), and the whole hilltop was surrounded by a ditch and palisade. The final phase of Site A would last into the Early Medieval period, being dated between the 4th and 7th CE, contemporary with the founding of Armagh. The site would be re-used in the medieval period, the Annals of Ulster recording that Níall Óg Ua Neill built a house for the poets of Ireland here in 1387, and a burial previously interpreted as a Romano-British priest being carbon dated to the post-medieval period. The site has long been considered a ceremonial and ritual centre, but more recently the figure-of-eight structures have been suggested to be 'temples' or 'shrines', though the meaning in use here is unclear, especially Site A, where related burials were once thought to be priests. Recent non-intrusive studies of the site have revealed a much greater number of features than previously recognised, showing that there is still a great deal to learn about this site.
